headline: A stalled offshore low opened a stormy week that peaked Thursday, with a brief weekend break.
summary:
Forecasters began the week saying a cold low aloft would stall offshore, partly blocked by high pressure to the north, and then merge into a broad dip in the Pacific jet stream. That would turn the pattern wet, windy and active, and this call held all week. The main change was timing. Coastal flooding concern moved up to Monday's high tide, then Tuesday, and the peak of the whole storm series settled on late Wednesday into Thursday. The strongest winds and heaviest rain were expected then. Some of the year's highest tides lined up with the storms, which kept coastal flooding the biggest worry. Snow levels stayed high, so rain fell at most elevations, but the North Cascades were expected to get heavy snow.

Once the strong storm wound down, attention turned to the weekend. A brief ridge of high pressure aloft was first floated as a break on Friday, then moved to the weekend, and by Wednesday the models agreed on it. It looks like light rain Friday, then a mostly quiet Saturday. The next change came Thursday, when forecasters dropped an earlier idea of a strong offshore storm on Sunday night. By Friday they were again watching a low that could bring strong winds Sunday night into Monday. They can't say how strong the winds will be because the models disagree on its track. High tides keep coastal flooding a concern into next week. Forecasters expect the storm track to shift south later in the week, which would mean somewhat quieter weather here.

turning_points.what: The coastal flooding concern moved up to Monday morning's high tide, and a coastal flood warning was issued for the Grays Harbor coast.
The peak of the stormy stretch was set for Thursday, and a Winter Storm Watch was added for the North Cascades.
Forecasters raised the expected peak coastal gusts to around 60 mph, and the models came to agree on a brief weekend break.
The possible strong offshore storm for Sunday night was dropped, and attention shifted to a Monday system whose track was uncertain.
